e7_s3: Hereditary breast and ovarian cancer syndrome
e7_s4_rationale: The patient has a family history of prostate cancer and a germline mutation in the MSH6 gene, which is a key component of the mismatch repair system and associated with Lynch syndrome. The presence of abnormal vaginal bleeding and the detection of a tumor also align with the increased risk of endometrial cancer seen in Lynch syndrome.

e7_s4_rejected.label: Endometrial cancer
e7_s4_rejected.why: While endometrial cancer is a possible diagnosis given the abnormal vaginal bleeding and tumor, it does not explain the family history of prostate cancer or the germline MSH6 mutation.

e7_s4_rejected.label: Endometrioid adenocarcinoma
e7_s4_rejected.why: This is a subtype of endometrial cancer but does not account for the genetic findings or family history of prostate cancer.

e7_s4_rejected.label: Atypical endometrial hyperplasia
e7_s4_rejected.why: This is a precursor to endometrial cancer but does not explain the genetic mutation or family history of prostate cancer.

e7_s4_rejected.label: Hereditary breast and ovarian cancer syndrome
e7_s4_rejected.why: This syndrome is associated with mutations in BRCA1 and BRCA2, not MSH6, and the family history of prostate cancer is more suggestive of Lynch syndrome.
